GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH & EDUCATION 
 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2584 
ANSWERED ON- 25/03/2022 
 
 
ALIGNING THE NAEP TO NEP 2020 TO ACHIEVE THE 2030 AGENDA 
 
 
2584 SHRI K.R. SURESH REDDY: 
 
  Will the MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government is planning to align the National Agricultural Education Policy (NAEP) 
with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which is based on five pillars, namely, Access, 
Equity, Quality, Affordability and Accountability to achieve the 2030 agenda; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (c):   To align the National Agricultural Education Policy (NAEP) with the National 
Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which is based on five pillars, namely, Access, Equity, Quality, 
Affordability and Accountability to achieve the  2030 agenda, the Indian Council of Agricultural 
Research (ICAR) has prepared a road map with a detailed timeline for implementation of NEP 
by Agricultural Universities (AUs).  "Implementation Strategy for National Education Policy-2020 in 
Agricultural Edu cation System". This may be accessed online at 
https://icar.gov.in/hi/file/14060/download?token=vVfizqOA.

GOVERNMENT OF I
NDIA

DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2585 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25/03/2022 
 
UTILIS
ATION OF FUNDS PROVIDED BY NABARD 
 
2585.    DR. C. M. RAMESH:   
 
Wil
l the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether NABARD has funded many agricultural projects in the State of Andhra Pradesh 
during the last three years, if so details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether all such projects are functional and clearance from appropriate authorities have 
been taken, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) whether loan received for the said purpose has been utilised for the intended purpose or 
diverted to some other projects, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (c):  NABARD provides support for infrastructure projects and various developmental 
& promotional  activities and projects for development and income generating activities in rural 
areas through various funds i.e. Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), NABARD 
Infrastructure Development Assistance (NIDA), Watershed Development Fund (WDF), Farm 
Sector Promotion Fund (FSPF) Tribal Development Fund (TDF), etc. The details with respect to 
assistance under various funds provided for projects in Andhra Pradesh are furnished below: 
 
(i) Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF): NABARD has sanctioned 
162 Integrated Agriculture labs and 46 Aquaculture Labs with a financial 
assistance of Rs. 150.34 crore under RIDF XXV (2019-20). The funds are being 
utilised as per the intended purpose.  
 
(ii) NABARD Infrastructure Development Assistance (NIDA):  Under NIDA, loan 
of Rs. 1931 crore has been sanctioned to Andhra Pradesh Water Resources 
Development Corporation for Completion of Chintalapudi Lift Irrigation Scheme. 
The utilisation is in line with the intended purpose for which it was sanctioned.  
 
136

(iii) F
arm Sector Promotion Fund (FSPF):   The FSPF is meant for supporting 
technology transfer, capacity building, etc, in the field of agriculture. During the 
last three years, 09 Detailed Project Report (DPR) based projects have been 
sanctioned to various agencies with a total grant assistance of Rs. 88.82 Lakhs. 
  
(iv) Watershed Development Fund (WDF):  Under WDF, grant support has been 
extended for development of Watersheds in drought prone districts in Andhra 
Pradesh. During the last three years, 19 Watershed projects have been sanctioned 
involving grant assistance of Rs. 14.23 crore.  
 
(v) Tribal Development Fund: Under TDF grant support is provided to tribal 
families for establishment of orchards (wadis) and support for other livelihood 
activities. For the FY 2019-20, 3 projects had been sanctioned with a total grant 
amount of Rs. 792.353 lakh, while in 2020-21, a total no of 4 projects had been 
sanctioned with grant assistance of Rs. 1111.38 lakh. For FY 2021-22, 2 projects 
have been sanctioned with grant amount of Rs. 618.647 lakh.  
 
(vi) Farmers’ Producer Organisation (FPO):   FPOs are farmers' collectives with 
membership comprising mainly of small and marginal farmers, formed with the 
objective to improve farmers’ returns. FPOs combine the spirit of cooperatives 
with the professional business outlook of a corporate to enable farmers 
professionally manage their farming activities and engage directly as a key player 
in the agri-value chain. Collectivization in farming through FPOs has emerged as 
a potential tool to transform agriculture into a sustainable enterprise by taking 
advantage of the economies of scale. 
 
The details of FPOs sanctioned in last three years in Andhra Pradesh are given below:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE) 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2586 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25th MARCH, 2022 
 
 
MEASURES TO REDUCE TRUCK TRANSIT TIME INTO BENAPOLE PORT IN 
BANGLADESH 
 
2586. SHRI MAHESH PODDAR:  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE & INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been a significant delay for Indian export trucks to  
cross into Benapole land port in Bangladesh, if so, the details of waiting period thereof; 
(b) the measures being taken by Government to reduce the waiting and transit time, the  
details thereof; 
(c) the value to trade and the number of trucks passing through the Petrapole -Benapole 
crossing, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether Government is deliberating upon opening add itional land ports for merchandise  
export into Bangladesh, if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
(a) :    There is no delay for Indian trucks to cross international border and enter Benapole Customs 
area from Petrapole. Let Export Order (LEO) is granted on the same day of goods registration and 
the trucks physically exit India within 24 hours; 
 (b) :    To further reduce transit time, Customs staff have been deputed 24x7 to enable faster 
clearances.  In addition, Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI) has initiated a tender process for 
construction of a 2 nd Cargo Gate at Petrapole  and provisioning for additional parking of 
approximately 500 vehicles at Integrated Check Post , Petrapole to reduce the waiting  and transit 
time; 
  
 
138

2

crossing are as under:

PRARAMBH-STARTUP INDIA INTERNATIONAL SUMMIT 
 
2587  SMT. SHANTA CHHETRI: 
 
Will the Minister of Commerce and Industry be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the progress report of 'Prarambh - Startup India International Summit' so far; 
 
(b)  to which extent has this initiative benifited the State of West Bengal in particular; and 
 
(c)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI SOM PARKASH) 
 
(a):  On 15th and 16th January 2021, the Government organised "Prarambh – Startup 
India International Summit" celebrating the 5th anniversary of the launch of the 
Startup India  Initiative. The Summit was hosted virtually for two days and 
brought together over 200 marquee speakers from across startup ecosystems 
within the country, Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi -Sectoral Technical and 
Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) member stat es as well as other 
international geographies.  
 
The Summit hosted 24 sessions covering all aspects of the innovation and 
entrepreneurship ecosystem. The sessions focused on sharing best practices, 
knowledge exchange workshops, multilateral incubator progr ams, promoting 
social innovation, startup ecosystems in India, startup success stories, industry-
academia partnership, international best practices, women entrepreneurship, 
inspiring youth for innovation and entrepreneurship, and much more. 
  
The Government also unveiled “Startup India: The Way Ahead” at the Summit 
which includes actionable plans for promotion of ease of doing business for 
startups, greater role of technology in executing various reforms, building 
capacities of stakeholders and enabling a digital Aatmanirbhar Bharat.  
 
The Summit also included a virtual startup showcase, closed-door B2B sessions 
and closed-door sessions on mobilizing domestic and global capital for Indian 
startups. 
 
During the Summit, various regulatory issues experienced by  the startup 
ecosystem were deliberated. Consequently, a number of regulatory reforms 
140

have been undertaken by the Government to ease doing of business by startups. 
These include: 
 
i. Ministry of Finance on 15th March, 2021 permitted non -government 
provident f unds, superannuation, and gratuity funds to invest up to 5 
percent of their investible surplus in Category I and II AIFs . This is a 
pivotal amendment in helping achieve financial stability in the startup 
ecosystem by allowing startups to access a higher pe rcentage of rupee 
capital. 
ii. Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India on 5 April 2021, 
allowed investments by insurance agencies in Fund of Funds (FoF), which 
would increase capital flow into AIFs via FoFs.  
iii. Ministry of Labour and Employment on 28th April 2021 allowed 
Employees Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) to invest its 5% of 
investible surplus into Category I and Category II AIFs. This change in 
investment pattern will expose sizeable domestic surplus generated in the 
nation towards the growth of Indian startup ecosystem. 
iv. Harmonization of the “Startup” definition across various regulatory and 
government bodies. 
v. The SEBI (Alternative Investment Fund) (Second Amendment) 
Regulations 2021 removed the list of restricted activities or sectors from 
the definition of Venture Capital Undertaking i.e. Category 1 AIFs can now 
invest in NBFCs. 
 
Furthermore, during the Summit, the Government announced creation of 
Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS). SISFS was launched on 1 st April 
2021. The Scheme has corpus of Rs. 945 crore for providing seed funding to 
eligible startups through eligible incubators across India. The ‘Call for 
Application’ for incubators under the Scheme was launched on 19th April 2021. 
As on 17 th March 2022, 76 incubators have been selected and a sum of Rs. 
295.75 crore have been approved as grant under the Scheme.  
 
During the Summit, the Government also announced the launch of Startup 
Champions program on Doordarshan bouquet of channels to highlight the 
innovations in the country. The first series of the program has been successfully 
concluded. The program was telecasted in both Hindi and English across 
Doordarshan network channels. It was a one-hour weekly program spread over 
12 weeks. 12 episodes have been  telecasted over a period of 3 months. The 
startups which have been part of this program have reported exponential 
increase in their overall visibility, demand for their products and even investor 
interest. 
 
The Summit Report, published by DPIIT on the Sta rtup India Portal, captures 
the key features and proceedings of the two-day summit. The same is available 
at the website of Startup India 
(https://www.startupindia.gov.in/content/dam/invest-
india/Templates/public/Startup%20India%20International%20Summit%20202
1%20Report_vf.pdf).  
  
141

(b) & (c):  The Summit was aimed at promoting entrepreneurship and exchange best 
practices for nurturing startup ecosystems across India including the State of 
West Bengal. Startups representing all states and UTs, including West Bengal 
were invited for the Startup Showcase during the Summit. The event received 
more than 1.2 Lakh registrations on the virtual platform from all States and UTs 
including the State of West Bengal and over 56 countries. Virtual Startup 
Showcase featured more than 1,100 high -quality innovations from across the 
country. More than 10,000 people visited and interacted with the showcasing 
startups. Additionally, 15 startups, 9 from India and 6 from the BIMSTEC 
member states, received an opportunity to interact  with the Hon’ble Prime 
Minister at the Grand Plenary session.

ALLOCATION AND DISTRIBUTION OF FUNDS TO STARTUPS 
 
2589. SHRI ABDUL WAHAB: 
SHRI JOSE K. MANI: 
 
Will the Minister of Commerce and Industry be pleased to state: 
 
 
(a)  whether Government has any data regarding number of Startups established across the 
country over last five years; 
 
(b)  if so, year-wise and State-wise details thereof including registered Startups; 
 
(c)  whether Government has any data regarding allocation and distribution of funds under 
Startup India scheme to provide funding support to Startups in the country; 
 
(d)  if so, year-wise and State-wise details thereof; 
 
(e)  list of companies registered with Government and became successful; 
 
(f)  whether Government has any plans to support those Startups who got shut down/are on 
verge of shutting down in last five years and during COVID-19 pandemic; and 
 
(g)  if so, details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI SOM PARKASH) 
 
(a) & (b):  The Government recognises  eligible entities as ‘Startups’ under Startup India 
initiative, launched in 2016, as per G.S.R. notification 127 (E). 66,359 startups have 
been recognised over the last five years including the current year up to 21st March 
2022. 
 
The year-wise and state-wise details of recognized startups across the country for 
the last five years as on 21st March 2022 are at Annexure I. 
  
(c) & (d):  The Government does not directly fund startups under Startup India initiative. To 
provide capital at various stages of business cycle of a startup, the Government, 
under Startup India initiative, is implementing Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) 
Scheme and Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS). 
  
144

The Fund of Funds for Startups Scheme was approved and established in 2016 with 
a corpus of Rs 10,000 crore, with contribution spread over the 14th and 15th 
Finance Commission cycle based on progress of implementation, to provide much-
needed boost to the Indian startup ecosystem and enable access to domestic capital. 
The FFS doe s not directly invest into startups. It invests into SEBI - registered 
Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), who in turn make investments into startups. 
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) is the operating agency for 
FFS. As on 28 th February 2022, Department has allocated Rs. 2791.29 crores to 
SIDBI and SIDBI has in turn committed Rs. 6,795 crore to 82 Alternative 
Investment Funds (AIFs), while Rs. 8,785 crore have been invested by supported 
AIFs in 574 startups. 
  
Year and state-wise allocation and drawdown of funds under FFS as on 21st March 
2022 are at Annexure II. 
  
The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) aims to provide financial assistance 
to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry 
and commerci alization. This would enable these startups to graduate to a level 
where they will be able to raise investments from angel investors or venture 
capitalists or seek loans from commercial banks or financial institutions. The funds 
under the Scheme are releas ed to startups through approved incubators. Rs. 945 
crore has been allocated under the Scheme for period of 4 years starting from 2021-
22.  
  
Year and state-wise allocation and approval of funds under SISFS as on 21st March 
2022 are at Annexure III. 
  
(e) to (g):  The information with respect to the success or failure of startups is not centrally 
maintained.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2591 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25th MARCH, 2022 
 
APPEAL AGAINST WTO RULING ON SUBSIDY ON SUGAR 
 
2591. SHRI V. VIJAYASAI REDDY:  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE & INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) how Ministry looks at the ruling of the Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) of the WTO  
against country’s sugar subsidy; 
(b) how our subsidies are prohibitive and the reasons behind asking India to withdraw the  
same; 
(c) the details of countries that have complained against our subsidies and reasons and  
justification thereof; 
(d) how can DSB say that Government is giving support price and reject India’s contention  
as it is not Government but sugar mills which are giving subsidy; and 
(e) whether Ministry is thinking of going in for appeal and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
(a) to (e):  Australia, Brazil and Guatemala filed a dispute challenging specific schemes of 
India for its sugar and sugarcane sector, before the World Trade Organisation (WTO).  
Accordingly, a dispute panel was established in WTO, which circulated its report on 14 
December 2021.  The panel has found that India provided domestic support to sugarcane 
producers over the permitted level under Agreement on Agriculture (AoA) of the WTO. The 
panel has also found that India provided prohibited export subsidies through specific schemes. 
It has recommended that India bring its WTO inconsistent measures into conformity with its 
obligations under the relevant Agreements. India has appealed against the panel report in the 
WTO on the ground that the panel findings are unreasoned, undermines logic and rationale, and 
are not supported by the WTO rules.

SURGE IN IMPORTS 
 
2594. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE & INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that many industries and their associations have expressed concerns  
at surge in imports, especially of metals and capital goods, from countries including 
Korea, Indonesia, Malaysia and Japan with whom India has signed Free Trade  
Agreements (FTAs); 
(b) if so, the details thereof and Government's response thereto ; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that domestic manufactures have been adversely affected and  
derailing 'Make in India' programme due to mis-using of bilateral FTAs; and 
(d) if so, Gove rnment's response thereto and the steps taken by Government to check  
unlawful imports for survival of domestic industry? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
(a) to (d): Representations from industry and their associations are received from time to time 
on surge in imports from ASEAN countries, Japan and Korea, which are examined in consultation 
with the concerned administrative Ministries/ Departments and other stakeholde rs and taken up 
with the respective trading partners under the existing institutional mechanism enshrined in the 
respective FTAs.  FTAs have inbuilt provisions to check any misuse of the FTA concessions, 
which inter-alia include strict compliance of the Rules of Origin, checking mis-declaration, if any, 
and taking trade remedial actions. The Government also reviews the provisions of the FTAs and 
their implications from time to time.  Some of these actions taken by the Government include 
measures related to trade remedies such as Safeguards Duties, Anti -dumping Duties and 
Countervailing Duties, in case of sufficient grounds of misuse and surge in imports causing serious 
injury to domestic producers.  Moreover, the Government has also restricted  imports of cer tain 
products.

(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether the proposed changes are being done for allowing foreign players to bid for  
LIC since LIC Act does not permit foreign investment; and 
 
(d)  whether it would contradict the stand of Government that LIC would be opened only 
for domestic investors or general public of the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI SOM PARKASH) 
 
(a) & (b): To promote Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), the Government has put in place 
an investor-friendly policy, wherein many sectors are open for 100% FDI under 
the automatic route. Further, the policy on FDI is reviewed on an ongoing basis, 
to ensure that India remains attractive & investor friendly destination. Changes 
are made in the policy after having detailed consultations with stakeholders 
including apex industry chamber s, associations, representatives of 
industries/groups and other organizations. Government has recently undertaken 
a number of reforms across sectors. In the past year, reforms in the FDI policy 
have been undertaken in sectors such as Insurance, Petroleum &  Natural Gas, 
Telecom etc. 
(c) & (d): There is no provision in the Insurance Act, 1938 or the Life Insurance 
Corporation Act, 1956 regarding foreign investment in the Life Insurance 
Corporation of India (LIC) or allowing investment into LIC only to domesti c 
investors or general public. As such, the framework applicable for foreign 
investment in LIC consists of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 
(“FEMA”), the rules and regulations made thereunder, and the FDI 
Policy. Accordingly, vide Press Note 1 (20 22 Series) dated 14.03.2022, 
Government has amended the FDI Policy to permit FDI up to 20% in LIC under 
the automatic route.

FUNDING OF TOCKLAI TEA RESEARCH INSTITUTE 
 
2599.  SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD BAISHYA:  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE & INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) the fund allocation after 2012 by Government to the Tocklai Tea Research Institute  
(TTRI) to boost the production and standardization of facilities; 
(b) the products made/invented so far by TTRI in the field of health, hygiene, environment  
and local agriculture; and 
(c) the blueprints prepared by Government to support the ongoing research in TTRI? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
(a) to (c): Tocklai Tea Research Institute (TTRI) is a research institute under the Tea Research 
Association (TRA).  The Tea Board supports research activities carried out by the Tea 
Research Association (TRA), Tocklai with a view to promote production and quality of 
tea.  Financial assistance of Rs.106.75 crore has been provided to TRA since 2012 -13 till 
21 March 2022.  
 
The research activities undertaken by TTRI are aimed at developing superior tea cultivars,  
plant protection through controlling pest & diseases, addressing pesticide residue problem, 
natural resource management and enhancement of quality. The products made/invented by 
TTRI are as under: 
 
(i) In the field of health and hygiene, antiviral activity of the a flavins (a major black tea 
polyphenol) against Hepatitis-C virus was demonstrated in human hepatoma cells in 
2017 and in silico studies on antiviral activity of Tea Bio actives against SARS-Cov-2 
was demonstrated in 2021. Tea bioactive based soft drinks and enriched drinking water 
formulations were developed in 2019. TTRI also developed iron filing extractor 
machine  for removing iron filings from made tea in tea factories.  To improve the 
quality of tea leaves, TR Agnext Fine Leaf count machine has been de veloped for 
counting of fine leaf with use of Artificial Intelligence technologies. 
161

(ii) In the field of environment & local agriculture, TTRI developed agro technology for 
organic tea production. Large scale production of biopesticides has also been 
developed at Tocklai.  TTRI also demonstrated drip irrigation & fertigation through 
drip with saving of 25% water and fertilizers in addition to saving application cost. 
Production technologies have been developed for diversified products like 
Black/Green Instant Tea, Black/Gree Tea Concentrate, Tea Premixes etc. Low cost tea 
dryer has been developed for small tea growers.  In addition, TTRI has released various 
machines like Rotorvane, Borbora continuous leaf conditioner, Tea breaker cum stalk 
separator etc. for use by the Tea industry.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2602. 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 25TH MARCH, 2022. 
 
JOB CREATION UNDER MAKE IN INDIA 
 
2602.  SHRI RAM CHANDER JANGRA: 
 
Will the Minister of Commerce and Industry be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of new additional jobs created under the 'Make in India' initiative started in 
year 2014 during the last five years, the details thereof, State-wise; and 
 
(b)  whether new Startups were also facilitated financially by Government under this  
initiative, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI SOM PARKASH) 
 
(a):   The 'Make in India' initiative was launched on 25th September, 2014 to facilitate 
investment, foster innovation, build best in class infrastructure, and make India 
a hub for manufacturing, design, and innovation. It is one of the unique 'Vocal 
for Local' initiatives that promoted India's manufacturing domain to the world.  
 
'Make in India' initiative has significant achievements and presently focuses on 
27 sectors under Make in India 2.0. Department for Promotion of Industry and 
Internal Trade (DPIIT) coord inates action plans for 15 manufacturing sectors, 
while Department of Commerce coordinates 12 service sector plans. Investment 
outreach activities are done through Ministries, State Governments and Indian 
Missions abroad for enhancing International co -operation and promoting both 
domestic and foreign investment in the country.  
 
As per Economic Survey 2021-22, in spite of covid-related disruptions there is 
trend of positive overall growth of gross value addition (GVA) in manufacturing 
sector. The total employment in this sector has increased from 57 million in the 
year 2017-18 to 62.4 million in the year 2019-20. 
 
The activities under Make in India initiative are also being undertaken by 
several Central Government Ministries/Departments and various State 
Governments. Ministries formulate action plans, programmes, schemes and 
policies for the sectors being dealt by them, while States also have their own 
schemes for attracting investments. 
167

(b):  Startup India initiative is a flagship initiative of Government of  India which 
aims to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and Startups in the 
country that will drive sustainable economic growth and generate large -scale 
employment opportunities. 
 
Two national level schemes are being implemented under Startu p India 
initiative for eligible startups to secure support and funding through: 
 
(i) Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) Scheme:  The Government has 
established FFS with corpus of Rs. 10,000 crore, to meet the funding needs of 
startups. DPIIT is the monitoring  agency and Small Industries Development 
Bank of India (SIDBI) is the operating agency for FFS. The total corpus of        
Rs. 10,000 crores are envisaged to be provided over the 14 th and 15th Finance 
Commission cycles based on progress of the Scheme and availability of funds. 
 
(ii) Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS):  The Scheme aims to provide 
financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, 
product trials, market entry and commercialization. It is estimated to support 
3,600 entrepreneurs through 300 incubators during the period 2021 to 2025.

BOOST TO EXPORTS FROM NORTH EAST REGION 
 
2603.  SHRI SANJAY SINGH:  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE & INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) the details regarding commodity exports from North East region during the last three  
years; 
(b) whether Government plans to boost the exports of various items from North East  
region; 
(c) if so, the details thereof along with the financial outlay of schemes/programmes being  
undertaken; and 
(d) the major impediments in boosting exports from the North East and the details of  
Government's plan to tackle it? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
(a) : The details of commodity exports from North East Region during last three years is at 
Annexure-I.  
(b) to (d):  Yes Sir.  Several steps and schemes have been devised to promote exports from 
North East Region. Some of the key schemes/int erventions taken to promote export 
infrastructure, improve market access and tackle other impediments are as below: 
 
i. In order to support the tea sector, Government of India has taken various initiatives 
through the Tea Board by way of providing financial a nd technical assistance to 
growers and the industry for new planting, re -plantation, rejuvenation, quality up-
gradation, value addition and market promotion. The Tea Development and 
Promotion Scheme (TDPS) has been approved for implementation from 2021 -22 
till 2025-26, where a key component is allotment of Rs.93.06 Cr for implementing 
a ‘Sector Specific Action Plan’ for North East for utilizing the potential of the 
region by boosting production and exports, with emphasis on organic tea exports. 
169

 
 
ii. ‘Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and 
Research & Development of Cardamom’ has been approved by the Department for 
the period 2021-22 to 2025-26. Under this scheme, specific allotment of Rs 8.50 Cr 
for NE Region has been made for FY 2021-22. Further, Spices Board has set up a 
network of 18 offices in NE States. The Board also has established the Regional 
Research Station of Indian Cardamom Research Institute (ICRI) at Tadong in 
Sikkim to undertake research on large cardamom.  
iii. For Agricultural products, Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export 
Development Authority (APEDA) has been organizing International Buyer -Seller 
Meet in North East to boost export for the region. APEDA also provides financial 
assistance through its Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) which aims to facilitate 
the exporters of Agri - products by providing assistance to exporters under the 
following components (i) Development of Export Infrastructure, (ii)Quality 
Development and (iii) Market development. Under  all the scheme components of 
APEDA for 2021-26 special financial focus has been laid down on all North eastern 
states by providing higher percentage of assistance i.e. upto 75% for all activities / 
components.  
iv. Under the Market Access Initiative (MAI) Scheme, financial support is provided to 
Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), Commodity Boards, Trade Bodies, etc. for 
various initiatives and activities, with the objective to develop trade, market 
intelligence and bu ild appropriate skill sets. The exporters from the NER are 
eligible for priority sector funding at the enhanced rate of 90% of the actual 
expenditure. MAI assistance of Rs.10.78 Crore has been approved to EPCs and 
Trade Bodies for undertaking export promot ion activities pertaining to the NER 
during FY 2021-22.  
v. Trade Infrastructure for Export Scheme (TIES) is being implemented from FY 
2017-18 for all States/UTs with the objective of assisting Central and State 
Government agencies for creation of appropriate  infrastructure for growth of 
exports. Under the scheme, Central Government assistance upto 80% of total equity 
is provided in the form of grant -in-aid in the total project cost for projects located 
in North Eastern States. The Scheme has been extended for the period FY 2021-22 
to 2025-26 with total financial outlay of Rs. 360 crores.  
vi. The Border Haats are set up in Tripura and Meghalaya under Memorandum of 
Understanding (MoU) with Bangladesh for promoting traditional system of 
marketing the local produce.  
 
170

vii. The Government of India has declared the Shellac & Forest Products Export 
Promotion Council (SHEFEXIL) as the nodal agency for export promotion from 
the North-Eastern states. 
viii. Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) hosted a meeting for 
the Department of Fisheries of North Eastern States to explore the possibilities of 
implementation of viable projects towards aquaculture development in these states. 
The states have been informed of the measures to be taken by them to increase 
production and boosting exports of Tilapia Fish.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2604. 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 25TH MARCH, 2022. 
 
NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF DESIGN IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
2604.  SHRI SUBHAS CHANDRA BOSE PILLI: 
SHRI VENKATARAMANA RAO MOPIDEVI: 
SHRI AYODHYA RAMI REDDY ALLA: 
 
Will the Minister of Commerce and Industry be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Central Government has approved detailed project report for construction  
of National Institute of Design (NID) at Andhra Pradesh and budget has been allocated; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(c)  whether Government has sanctioned the entire approved budget for the establishment  
of NID, Andhra Pradesh; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI SOM PARKASH) 
 
(a) to (d):  Yes Sir. The Government has approved the budget and Detailed Project  
Report for construction of NID, Andhra Pradesh. The total budget approved for 
construction of National Institute of Design (NID) Andhra Pradesh is Rs 100.38 
Crore. Rs 0.70 Crore was spent on Pre -construction expenses such as survey 
and boundary wall. The e ntire remaining amount has been sanctioned and 
released - Rs 93.18  Crore to National Building Construction Corporation 
(NBCC), the project execution agency; and Rs 6.50 Crore to NID Ahmedabad 
for supply of machinery, equipment and library books.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE) 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2605 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25th MARCH, 2022 
 
PRE-LEGISLATIVE CONSULTATION POLICY ON TEA (PROMOTION AND 
DEVELOPMENT) BILL, 2022 
 
2605.  SHRI DIGVIJAYA SINGH:  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE & INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy was formulated by Central Government in  
year 2014, if so, details thereof; 
(b) how many Bills were introduced by Government from May 2014 onwards in Parliament 
and in how many cases, this policy was adopted; 
(c) whether the draft of any Bill under the said policy is required to be kept in the public  
domain for at least 30 days, if so, whether Tea (Promotion and Development) Bill, 2022 
has been kept in public domain for the said period, if not, reasons therefor; and 
(d) whether Government has held discussions with all stakeholders/trade unions of tea  
industry? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL) 
(a) and (b): The Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy was formulated by the Committee of 
Secretaries in the year 2014 for implementation by the Ministries/Departments of the Central 
Government before finalizing any legislative proposal. As p er information received from 
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs a total of 393 Bills have been introduced in both the 
Houses of Parliament from May, 2014 to 21.3.2022. The Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy 
is available at https://legislative.gov.in. 
 
(c) and (d):  Yes Sir, as per the  provisions of Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy, the draft  of 
any Bill under the said policy is required to be kept in the public  
domain for at least 30 days. Accordingly, the Tea (Promotion and Development) Bill, 2022 
has been placed in public domain from 10.01.2022 to 09.04.2022 seeking comments from 
public/stakeholders. Consultation meetings have been held with individual stakeholders 
(exporters, growers, traders, buyers etc.) an d associations of exporters/small tea 
growers/traders/manufacturers etc. and tea workers unions.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2607  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25TH MARCH, 2022 
 
CONNECTIVITY OF GRAM PANCHAYATS IN JHARKHAND WITH 
BROADBAND AND WI-FI HOTSPOTS 
 
2607 # SHRI DEEPAK PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of optical fibre cables laid under the National Optical Fibre Network 
project till date and the timeline fixed for achieving the remaining target; 
 
(b)  the number and details of Gram Panchayats connected with broadband and Wi -Fi 
hotspots under the above project in Jharkhand till date; and 
 
(c)  the number of Gram Panchayats in Jharkhand which are yet to be connected under the 
above project? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN) 
 
(a) BharatNet (earlier known as National Optical Fibre Network) project is implemented 
in a phased manner to provide broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats (GPs) in the 
country, including Jharkhand. As on 28.02.2022, total 5,67,941 km Optical Fibre Cable 
(OFC) has been laid and 1,72,361 GPs (1,68,010 GPs on OFC and 4,351 GPs on satellite) 
have been made Service Ready in the country. The scope of BharatNet has been recently 
extended up to all inhabited  villages beyond GPs in the country. The timeline of the 
BharatNet project is 2025. 
 
(b) & (c) The Phase-II of the BharatNet in Jharkhand is implemented under State-led 
model through the State Government under which, 1656 GPs have been made Service Ready 
out of about 1678 planned GPs. Further, 2 GPs have been made Service Ready on Satellite 
media out of 10 planned GPs. Under Phase-I, a total number of 2707 GPs were taken up for 
implementation through Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL), out of which 
2596 GPs have been made Service Ready. In total, 4254 GPs have been made Service Ready, 
out of planned 4395 GPs in Jharkhand, as on 28.02.2022, and 141 GPs are yet to be made 
Service Ready. 
 
The work of providing broadband facility (Wi-Fi hotspots and Fibre to the Home 
connections) in Phase-I GPs is implemented with funding from Universal Service Obligation 
Fund (USOF). As on 28.02.2022, Wi-Fi hotspots have been installed under BharatNet Phase-
I in 2383 GPs in Jharkhand. 
BharatNet Phase-II in Jharkhand is implemented by the State Government, which is 
also responsible for its utilization. However, no Wi-Fi hotspots have been installed under 
Phase-II so far.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2610  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25TH MARCH, 2022 
 
BROADBAND FOR DANTA IN BANASKANTHA DISTRICT 
 
2610 SHRI HARSHVARDHAN SINGH DUNGARPUR: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether BharatNet project is envisaged in Gram Panchayats and villages of Danta of 
Banaskantha district to provide high speed internet/ broadband; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) as per Ce nsus 2011 of the Ministry, the coverage and level of bandwidth of antennas 
installed in Danta; and 
 
(d) the steps taken/ proposed to be taken by Government to improve the mobile/ internet 
connectivity in the villages? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN) 
 
(a) & (b) BharatNet project is implemented in a phased manner to provide broadband 
connectivity to all Gram Panchayats (GPs) in the country, including all GPs of Danta of 
Banaskantha District of Gujarat.  
 
 The Phase-II of BharatNet in Gujarat is implemented under State -led model through the 
State Government under which, 7608 GPs have been made Service Ready out of 7668 
planned GPs. Further, 22 GPs have been made Service Ready on Satellite media  out of 26 
planned GPs. Under Phase -I, a total number of 6593 GPs were taken up for implementation 
through RailTel Corporation of India Limited, out of which 6489 GPs have been made 
Service Ready. In total, 14,119 GPs have been made Service Ready in Gujara t, as on 
28.02.2022. All the 56 GPs in Danta Taluka/ Block of Banaskantha District have been made 
Service Ready. The scope of BharatNet has been recently extended up to all inhabited 
villages beyond GPs in the country. 
 
(c)  As per census 2011, Danta Taluka/Block of Banaskantha District of Gujarat  has 182 
villages. As per the information provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs), 166 villages 
of Danta Taluka/Block are covered with mobile connectivity, out of which 158 have high -
speed mobile internet through 3G/4G technology Base Transceiver Stations (BTS)/Antennas.  
(d)  Broadband/Internet services are provided in a phased manner by the Government and 
Telecom Services Provider (TSPs) in the uncovered villages of the country. The Government, 
with funding from Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF), has schemes namely 
Comprehensive Telecom Development Plan for North Eastern Region, Left Wing Extremism 
(LWE) Affected Area schemes, Aspirational Districts Schemes, Comprehensive Telecom 
Development Plan for Islands, etc. to extend Broadband/Internet services through mobile 
connectivity to the uncovered villages. 
 
The infrastructure created under BharatNet project can be utilized for provisioning of 
broadband/internet services through Wi-Fi Hotspots, Fibre to the Home (FTTH) connections, 
leased lines, dark fibre, backhaul to mobile towers, etc.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2611  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25TH MARCH, 2022 
 
PARALLEL TELEPHONE EXCHANGE IN KERALA 
 
2611  SHRI M.V. SHREYAMS KUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government was aware of a parallel telephone exchange that was working at 
Kozhikode in Kerala; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, including the background of operators of the exchange and  
their modus operandi; 
 
(c)  whether Government had taken any action against the illegal exchange; 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof including the names of people who have been booked for 
illegal and anti-national activities; and 
 
(e)  whether these paralle l exchanges had any contact with India’s neighboring countries 
like China and Pakistan? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN) 
 
(a)  The required intelligence was provided by Kerala Police and subsequently six 
locations in Kozhikode were raided by Kerala Police on 1 st July 2021 with the support of 
Kerala License Service Area (LSA) field unit of Department of Telecommunications (DoT). 
 
(b)  Illegal telecom setups were found working at six locations in Kozhikode. These 
premises were having clandestine telecom setup using the Voice over Internet Protocol 
(VoIP) technique for bypassing the licensed International Long Distance Operator’s (ILDOs) 
networks and using mobile telecom networks of Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) for 
distributing these calls to the mobile / wire line customers across India.  
 
(c)  All equipment of clandestine telecom setups including Subscriber Identity Modules 
(SIM), VoIP Gateways etc. were seized by the Kerala Police. All telecom resources have 
been dis connected by TSPs concerned. Further, all TSPs have been instructed to monitor 
their network for any illegal telephone exchange activities, including the in -roaming mobile 
numbers for preventing the misuse.  
 
(d)   As per the information received from the Kerala Police, two persons named Jurais P 
and Ibrahim Pullattil were arrested. Lookout notice has been issued against four persons 
named Shabeer, Abdul Gafoor, Krishnaprasad and Niyas. 
 
(e)  The charge sheet has not yet been prepared by the Investigation o fficer of Kerala 
Police.

(c)  if so, how Ministry is pushing further to take IPPB to doorsteps of rural people 
through Postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks; and

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2615 FOR 25/03/2022 REGARDING SALIENT 
FEATURES OF INDIA POST PAYMENTS BANK 
Current products and services offered by India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) are as under: 
 Paperless & Instant account opening 
 Savings accounts for citizens including Aadhaar  Seeding for DBT (Direct 
Benefit Transfer) beneficiaries 
 Current Accounts for merchants 
 Virtual Debit Card 
 Cash Deposit/ Cash Withdrawal services  
 Domestic Money Transfer services – Immediate Payment Service (IMPS), National 
Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT ), Real Time Gross Settlement  (RTGS), Unified 
Payment Interface (UPI) 
 Bill Payment services - Bill payment of utility bills, (Direct -to-Home) DTH/Mobile 
recharges, EMI (Equated Monthly Instalment) payments, insurance etc. 
 Insurance services for IPPB custom ers – Life, Health, Vehicle insurance & Pradhan 
Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) 
 Post Office Savings Account (POSA) linkage with IPPB accounts 
 Online Payment for Post Office Savings schemes – Public Provident Fund (PPF), 
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSA), Recurring Deposit (RD) 
 Digital Life Certificate (DLC) services – Facilitate submission of DLC for any 
pensioners of central/state/ Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) 
 Aadhaar based services – Mobile Number update in Aadhaar for any citizen and Child 
Enrolment services for any child (0 - 5-year-old) 
 Cash Management services – Collection of dues from customers of corporates/ 
government bodies

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2616  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25TH MARCH, 2022 
 
REVENUE EARNED BY POST OFFICES 
 
2616 SHRI RAMKUMAR VERMA: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether there has been a decrease in the revenue earned by India Post due to COVID19 
pandemic and if so, the details thereof and the steps taken by Government to improve the revenue; 
 
(b)  whether there is any proposal of diversifying the business of India Post into more eCommerce 
and other value -added services by leveraging its workforce and vast postal network to increase the 
revenue and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c)  the other steps taken by Government to strengthen and boost the income of India Post? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN) 
 
 
(a)  Yes Sir, There had been a temporary dip in the revenues earned by the Department in 
2020-21 owing to Covid  19 pandemic. The department is making continuous efforts to 
increase the revenue. Department has made a net addition of around 1 crore Post Office 
Savings scheme  accounts in current Financial Year. New tie -ups have also been done with 
Government Organizations like Government e -Market place, Election Commission of India, 
Traffic Police Departments etc for Speed Post and parcel business. Also Common Service 
Centres are now functioning in more than 1.06 lakh post offices. 
 
(b)  Yes sir. Parcel services of th e Department have been rationalized and ‘Cash on 
Delivery’ was introduced as a value addition to parcel services to cater to the need of 
eCommerce market and generate additional revenue for the Department. A robust 
technological platform has also been prov ided for booking, processing and delivery of mails 
and parcels. Further, Department is also using Postman Mobile application to provide real 
time delivery update to the customers . Additionally, Department facilitates the customers 
through SMS alerts regarding status of articles. Application Programme Interface integration 
has also been provided to the eCommerce customers for seamless data exchange. In the 
recent past, Department has set up dedicated bulk mail/ Parcel processing centres and 
established Nodal Delivery centres for mechanisation of the Parcel delivery with a focused 
approach to cater eCommerce market. 
 
(c)  In order to generate additional revenue, Department regularly review its offerings and 
take appropriate action including introduction of new products and services to offer value 
additions to make them more customer and business centric. Department in tie - up with 
Government organisations is providing various citizen centric services viz. Aadhar Enrolment 
and updation facilities,  Post Office Passport Seva Kendras, Passenger Reservation facilities, 
Digital Life Certificates etc.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2618  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25TH MARCH, 2022 
 
LOW INTERNET CONNECTIVITY IN RURAL AREAS 
 
2618 #  SMT. GEETA ALIAS CHANDRAPRABHA: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total coverage of internet connectivity in rural areas of the country at present, the 
details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether it is a fact that even today, people in most of the rural areas are depri ved of 
internet services; and 
 
(c)  the steps being taken by Government to increase the internet connectivity coverage? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN) 
 
(a) & (b)  Internet / broadband connectivity is being provided in rural areas by the 
Licensed Service Providers through wireless mobile and fixed wireline connections. As per 
data provided by Telecom Service Providers and field units of Department of 
Telecommunications, it is estimated that out of 5,97,618 inhabited villages (as per Census 
2011) in the country, 5,58,537 villages have mobile wireless broadband coverage. 
 
(c)  Following steps have been taken by the Government for enhancing internet/broadband 
connectivity coverage in the country: 
 
(i) National Broadband Mission was launched on 17 th December, 2019 with a 
vision to fast track growth of digital communications infrastructure, bridge the digital 
divide, facilitate digital empowerment and inclusion, and provide affordable and 
universal access of broadband for all.  
(ii) In its endeavour t o provide high speed internet/broadband connectivity, 
BharatNet project is envisaged in all the Gram Panchayats (GPs) and villages of the 
country.  
(iii) To enhance proliferation of internet/broadband services in the country, Prime 
Minister Wireless Access  Network Interface (PM -WANI) framework has been 
introduced.  
(iv) Various schemes are implemented under Universal Service Obligation Fund 
(USOF) to enhance mobile broadband services in the rural and remote areas of the 
country including North Eastern Regio n (NER), areas affected by Left Wing 
Extremism (LWE), Border areas, Aspirational Districts and Island Territories.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2620  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25TH MARCH, 2022 
 
CONVERSION OF DUES FROM TELECOM OPERATORS AS EQUITY STAKES 
 
2620  SHRI JOHN BRITTAS: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government has decided to convert pending dues from 
telecom operators as equity stakes in respective companies; 
 
(b)  if so, the amount to be converted and the equity to be obtained; 
 
(c)  the procedure applied for deciding on the share price; and 
 
(d)  whether Government would hold on to the shares so acquired or disinvest the same? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN) 
 
(a) Department of Telecom, with the approval of the Union Cabinet Dated 15.09.2021, had 
given an option of moratorium of up to four years on annual deferred spectrum payments and the 
annual installment of Adjusted Gross Revenue related dues as determined payable vide Supreme 
Court order dated 01.09.2020 to eligible Telecom Service Providers (TSPs).  As approved by the 
Union Cabinet, an option for conversion of interest amount into equity, arising out of protection 
of Net Present Value (NPV) of the aforesaid dues for the moratorium period, was also given. 
 
(b) to (d)  M/s Vodafone Idea Ltd. (VIL) has exercised its option for converting its interest 
liabilities into equity.  As per Cabinet decision, Ministry of Finance shall finalize the procedure, 
method, rate of conversion, mix of equ ity and preferential capital (if any), in compliance with 
SEBI and other relevant guidelines.  Government can sell these shares at appropriate time and 
thereby receive the amount due.

PHONE TRACING UNDER CEIR 
 
2621  DR. NARENDRA JADHAV: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of mobile phones lost and stolen, including reprogrammed mobile handsets, that 
have been traced till now under the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR), the State-wise details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  whether it is a fact that Government is sharing data with private entities under CEIR, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
 
(c)  the extent of the data that is being shared with private entities under CEIR, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN)

Mumbai and Maharashtra licensed service areas (LSAs) in a phased manner to facilitate 
blocking and tracing of lost and stolen mo bile phones. As per the reports from CEIR system, 
the request for blocking of 169667, 8315 and 1184 8 International Mobile Equipment Identity

manufacturers and mobile phone subscr ibers have a limited access as per their defined roles

manufacturers about genuineness of IMEI during import of consignment of mobile phones 
etc.

RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2623  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25TH MARCH, 2022 
 
UNSOLICITED AND OBSCENE MESSAGES 
 
2623  SMT. ROOPA GANGULY: 
 
Will the Minister of Communications be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether there are unsolicited and obscene messages sent from MG650500; and 
 
(b)  the details of steps taken by the Ministry to stop such messages into circulation? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS  
(SHRI DEVUSINH CHAUHAN) 
 
(a) The header i.e. “MG650500” does not belong to any Telecom Service Provider (TSP). 
As per the directions issued by TRAI in this regard, the first two letters in a header represent 
TSP name and License Service Area(LSA)name respectively. Accordingly, the fir st letter 
“M” indicates Telecom Service Provider as MTNL, and Second Letter “G” indicates 
Licensed Service Area as Gujarat. Since MTNL does not operate in Gujarat, the “MG” prefix 
in the header “MG650500” does not belong to any of the TSP as such.  
 
(b) To curb the menace of Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC), TRAI has 
issued the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations -2018 
(“TCCCPR-2018”) on 19th July- 2018, which put in place a framework for controlling UCC.  
Under these regulations, TRAI has imposed Financial disincentives (FDs) of 
Rs.34,99,98,000/-for Quarter Ending June, 2020. F urther, Show Cause Notices (SCNs) have 
been issued upto Quarter Ending June, 2021.  
 
 The Unified License of DoT has a provision which bars/ pro hibits carriage of obscene 
messages in Clause 38.1 of chapter-V of  Part-I of License Agreement, which is given below: 
 
"Carriage of objectionable, obscene, unauthorized or any other content, messages or 
communications infringing copyright and intellectual  property right etc., in any form, 
in the network is not permitted as per established laws of the country. Once specific 
instances of such infringement are reported to the Licensee by the 
enforcement agencies/Licensor, the Licensee shall take necessary measures to prevent 
carriage of such messages in its network immediately."

HUGE PENDENCY OF REFUND OF DEPOSITS TO CONSUMERS

consumers who have surrendered landline connections, are pending with MTNL/BSNL for 
clearance; 
 
(b)  if so, their number upto 31 January, 2022 and the average duration for which they are 
pending and the reasons thereof; 
 
(c)  whether any rules or departmental order have been laid down in the matter and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  the steps that are going to be taken to expedite refund of pending deposits? 
 
ANSWER

UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2628 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25.03.2022 
FOOD INFLATION 
2628 SHRI SUJEET KUMAR: 
SHRI V. VIJAYASAI REDDY: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that food inflation in the country has increased;
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the details of consumer price index inflation from
June 2016 to June 2021;(c) the reasons as to why food inflation has increased;
(d) whether Government has taken any steps to keep food inflation in check; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE  
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY) 
(a) to (e) Food inflation measured by Consumer Food Price Index (CPFI) fluctuates over a period
time as the prices of agri-horticultural commodities are volatile as they tend to get affected by several
factors, such as mismatch in demand and supply, seasonality, supply chain constraints, artificial
shortage created by hoarding and black marketing, rise in international prices etc. Sometimes slight
disruptions in supply chain or damage due to heavy rains leads to spike in prices of agri-horticultural
commodities. The details of consumer price index inflation from June 2016 to June 2021 are given at
Annexure.
Taking into account price trends, the Government takes various measures from time to time to 
augment domestic availability and stabilize prices of essential food commodities. These steps, inter 
alia, include releases from the buffer to cool down prices, imposition of stock limits, monitoring of 
stocks declared by entities to prevent hoarding and also requisite changes in trade policy instruments 
like rationalization of import duty, changes in import quota, restrictions on exports of the commodity 
etc. 
In May, 2021 advisories were issued to States/UTs to monitor prices of essential food 
commodities and to ensure disclosure of pulses stocks held by millers, importers and traders under 
the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. Imposition of stock limit on all pulses except Moong was 
notified on 2.7.21. Thereafter, an amended order was issued on 19.7.21 imposing stock limits on four 
pulses, namely, Tur, Urad, Masur, Chana for a period up to 31.10.2021. 
230

 To improve availability and stabilise prices of pulses, the Government had allowed import of 
Tur, Urad and Moong under ‘Free category’ w.e.f 15.5.2021 till 31.10.2021 in order to ensure smooth 
and seamless imports. The Free regime was thereafter extended in respect of Tur and Urad till 
31.3.2022. This policy measure has been supported with facilitation measures and close monitoring 
of its implementation by the concerned Departments/organisations. The import policy measures have 
resulted in substantial increase in import of Tur, Urad and Moong as compared to the corresponding 
period for the past two years. In order to soften the impact of higher international prices on domestic 
consumers, the Government reduced duty on Masur to zero till September 30, 2022 and waived off 
the penalty on pulses import consignments from methyl bromide phased out countries for not being 
fumigated with methyl bromide in the country of origin till June 30, 2024. To augment the 
availability of pulses in the market, 3 Lakh Metric Ton of Chana stock has been released between 
June and August, 2021 through open market sales and to stabilize prices, futures trading in Chana has 
been suspended from August 16, 2021. State Governments have been supplied pulses from the buffer 
on an ongoing basis for their nutrition and welfare programmes.  
  In order to stabilize retail prices of onion, a buffer stock of 2.08 LMT had been built in 2021-
22. Open market releases of onion from the buffer were targeted towards States/Cities where prices 
were increasing.
 Releases were also made in source markets to augment the availability in key mandis 
and thereby reduce retail prices. States/UTs had also been offered onion at Rs.21/kg ex-storage 
locations. 
 
  In order to improve the domestic availability of edible oils and to keep prices under control, 
the Government has rationalized the duty structure on edible oils by reducing the effective duties. As 
per the notification dated 14.10.2021, the total duty on crude palm oil has been reduced from 22.5% 
to 7.5%, and on crude soyabean oil and sunflower oil it has been reduced from 22.5% to 5%. The 
basic duty on RBD palmolein, refined soyabean oil and refined sunflower oil has been reduced from 
32.5% to 17.5%. Thereafter, the basic duty on refined palm oil has been further reduced from 17.5% 
to 12.5% w.e.f 21.12.2021 and duty on crude palm oil reduced from 7.5% to 5% w.e.f 13.2.2022. 
Futures trading in essential commodities relating to food security had been suspended to curb 
speculative trading. Stock limits on edible oils and oilseeds have been imposed for a period upto 
30.06.2022 to prevent hoarding. 
 
  Further, the Government has issued advisory to States/UTs to set up the State-level Price 
Stabilisation Fund (PSF) corpus with central assistance, and has requested States which have set up 
the Fund already, to make appropriate interventions for cooling down retail prices of essential food 
commodities.

HALLMARKING OF GOLD JEWELLERY 
2636 SMT. JHARNA DAS BAIDYA: 
(OIH) 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has taken any step to make hallmarking of gold jewellery mandatory in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of hallmarking centres functioning in the country at present;
(d) whether any step has been taken by Government to check the sale of inferior quality jewellery;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE  
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY) 
(a)  & (b)    : Yes, Sir. Hallmarking has been made mandatory from 23 June, 2021 for 14, 18, & 
22 
carat of gold jewellery / artefacts in 256 districts of the country where there  is at least one Assaying 
and Hallmarking Centre (AHC). 
(c) : As on 20 March, 2022, 1060 hallmarking centres are functional in the country. 
(d) & (e)  : Yes, Sir. The Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID)-based system of 
hallmarking has been introduced as it was felt necessary that with hallmarking becoming mandatory, the 
credibility of the hallmark put on every piece of jewellery had to be ensured along with a robust system 
of real-time monitoring of the entire process. Under HUID, a unique six digit alphanumeric code is put 
on each gold jewellery / artifacts item along with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) logo and purity 
grade mark. 
BIS has developed the provision to verify HUID through the BIS CARE App- the official mobile 
application of BIS. The “Verify HUID” feature can be utilized to verify the purity of the gold jewellery 
items bearing a HUID number before purchase. Thus, the consumers can be assured of the authenticity 
of the HUID marked gold jewellery / artifacts items using the BIS Care Mobile App. 
247

Also, regular audit of assaying and hallmarking centres and market surveillance of BIS registered 
jewellers is undertaken to ensure that they comply to the requirement of BIS hallmarking scheme. 
Testing of random market samples drawn from registered jewellers is carried out to ensure the purity of 
hallmarked gold 
jewellery / artifacts is as per the marked purity on the article. In case of failure, action is 
taken both against the AHC who has hallmarked the article and the jeweler who has got the article 
hallmarked.

UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2639 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 25.03.2022 
RISE IN PRICES OF ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES 
2639 SHRI M. SHANMUGAM:
 SHRI Y. S. CHOWDARY: 
SHRI P. BHATTACHARYA: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is rise in prices of essential commodities in the last two years and in the
current year;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor, year-wise ;
(c) measures taken to control higher inflation to give relief to the common people;
(d) the reasons for higher food prices, especially in oil and fats categories, despite bumper
harvest in the country; and
(e) the efforts made to stabilize the economy, the details thereof?
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE  
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY) 
(a) to (e). The Government monitors the retail and wholesale prices of 22 essential food commodities
submitted by the 179 price monitoring centres that have been set up with Central assistance by State
Governments and UT Administrations across the country. The All India retail prices of 22 essential
commodities fluctuated in last two year and current year. The detail is at Annexure.
Prices of essential food commodities are volatile and tend to get affected by several factors, such as 
mismatch in demand and supply, seasonality, supply chain constraints, artificial shortage created by 
hoarding and black marketing, rise in international prices etc. Sometimes slight disruptions in supply 
chain or damage due to heavy rains leads to spike in prices of agri-horticultural commodities. 
Taking into account price trends, the Government takes various measures from time to time to 
augment domestic availability and stabilize prices of essential food commodities. These steps, inter 
alia, include releases from the buffer to cool down prices, imposition of stock limits, monitoring of 
stocks declared by entities to prevent hoarding as also requisite changes in trade policy instruments like 
rationalization of import duty, changes in import quota, restrictions on exports of the commodity etc. 
251

 
 
  In May, 2021 advisories were issued to States/UTs to monitor prices of essential food 
commodities and to ensure disclosure of pulses stocks held by millers, importers and traders under the 
Essential Commodities Act, 1955. Imposition of stock limit on all pulses except Moong was notified on 
2.7.21. Thereafter, an amended order was issued on 19.7.21 imposing stock limits on four pulses, 
namely, Tur,Urad, Masur, Chana for a period up to 31.10.2021. 
  To improve availability and stabilise prices of pulses, the Government had allowed import of 
Tur, Urad and Moong under ‘Free category’ w.e.f 15.5.2021 till 31.10.2021 in order to ensure smooth 
and seamless imports. The Free regime was thereafter extended in respect of Tur and Urad till 
31.3.2022. This policy measure has been supported with facilitation measures and close monitoring of 
its implementation by the concerned Departments/organisations. The import policy measures have 
resulted in substantial increase in import of Tur, Urad and Moong as compared to the corresponding 
period for the past two years. In order to soften the impact of higher international prices on domestic 
consumers, the Government reduced duty on Masur to zero till September 30, 2022 and waived off the 
penalty on pulses import consignments from methyl bromide phased out countries for not being 
fumigated with methyl bromide in the country of origin till June 30, 2024. To augment the availability 
of pulses in the market, 3 Lakh Metric Ton of Chana stock has been released between June and August, 
20
21 through open market sales and to stabilise prices, futures trading in Chana has been suspended 
from August 16, 2021. State Governments have been supplied pulses from the buffer stock on an 
ongoing basis for their nutrition and welfare programmes.  
  In order to stabilise retail prices of onion, a buffer stock of 2.08 LMT had been built in 2021-22. 
Open market releases of onion from the buffer were targeted towards States/Cities where prices were 
increasing.
 Releases were also made in source markets to augment the availability in key mandis and 
thereby reduce retail prices. States/UTs had also been offered onion at Rs.21/kg ex-storage locations. 
  In order to improve the domestic availability of edible oils and to keep prices under control, the 
Government has rationalized the duty structure on edible oils by reducing the effective duties. As per 
the notification dated 14.10.2021, the total duty on crude palm oil has been reduced from 22.5% to 
7.5%, and on crude soyabean oil and sunflower oil it has been reduced from 22.5% to 5%. The basic 
duty on RBD palmolein, refined soyabean oil and refined sunflower oil has been reduced from 32.5% 
to 17.5%. Thereafter, the basic duty on refined palm oil has been further reduced from 17.5% to 12.5% 
w.e.f 21.12.2021 and duty on crude palm oil reduced from 7.5% to 5% w.e.f 13.2.2022. Futures trading 
in essential commodities relating to food security had been suspended to curb speculative trading. 
Stock limits on edible oils and oilseeds have been imposed for a period upto 30.06.2022 to prevent 
hoarding. 
  Further, the Government has issued advisory to States/UTs to set up the State-level Price 
Stabilisation Fund (PSF) corpus with central assistance, and has requested States which have set up the 
Fund already, to make appropriate interventions for cooling down retail prices of essential food 
commodities.
